title: SLA Sourcing Snapshot for Enterprise Architects
body:
Purpose: quick, pragmatic briefing for platform architects and procurement partners evaluating dedicated inference capacity. Focus: how to translate engineering requirements (isolation, predictable throughput) into procurement asks and negotiable SLA clauses.

Audience: platform architects, procurement, solutions engineering, legal (SaaS SOW owners). Keep this as a one-pager + expandable script for field reps.

High-level framing (30s):
- Customers buy dedicated capacity to guarantee tail latency and throughput for real-time applications and to get strong isolation controls for compliance and data governance.
- Procurement wants clear measurables (MTTR, uptime by route/model, p95/p99 latency envelopes) and defined remedies. Engineering cares about deterministic per-request performance and failover behavior.

Key buyer problems we solve (word-for-word to use in talks):
- "We need predictable token throughput for customer-facing latency SLAs without noisy neighbors."
- "We need isolation so we can attest to auditors that sensitive prompts and logs are not shared across tenants."
- "We need a clear outage playbook — how does the vendor fall back and what are the RTO/RPO equivalents for inference?"

Procurement-ready asks (short list to include in RFPs / RFIs):
1) Throughput guarantees: specify sustained tokens/sec per reserved unit and p95/p99 latency targets at typical seq lengths.
2) Isolation model: single-tenant GPU pools, encrypted in-use KV cache, separate logging pipelines, audited access controls.
3) Capacity burst and throttling thresholds: guaranteed burst window (e.g., 30 minutes/day at 2x capacity) and defined throttling backoff behavior.
4) Escalation & remediation: time-to-first-response, root-cause windows, credit calculations for SLA breaches.
5) Model variant fallbacks: acceptable compatibility matrix and performance delta caps when automatic fallback runs.
6) Security & compliance attestations: KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2/ISO evidence, and on-prem deployment options.

Negotiation playbook (field script bullets):
- If asked for unlimited burst: propose bounded burst (30–60 min/day) + paid burst add-on.
- If customer demands p99 across all seq lengths: ask for profile baseline (typical seq length) and offer tiered p99 bands with price.
- When they insist on single-GPU tenancy: explain price delta, highlight multi-tenant with strong isolation controls as lower-cost alternative.

Procurement scoring rubric (one-pass table you can paste into spreadsheets):
- Criteria (weight): Throughput predictability (30), Isolation guarantees (25), SLA remedies (15), Compliance evidence (10), Support & escalation (10), Price & commercial flexibility (10).
- Scoring guidance: 0–5 per criterion. Multiply by weight, normalize to 100. Use as tie-breaker vs competitors.

Suggested SLA language snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- "Vendor guarantees sustained throughput of >= {X} tokens/sec per reserved capacity unit at sequence length {Y}, measured over rolling 10-minute intervals. Measured p95 latency shall be <= {A} ms and p99 latency shall be <= {B} ms."
- "Isolation: production traffic for customer will run in single-tenant pools or logically isolated execution environments with segregated logs and KV caches; no cross-tenant memory sharing is permitted."
- "Remedies: for any monthly uptime below {SLA}% credits will be issued as follows: [tiered credit schedule]. Credits are customer’s sole and exclusive remedy."

Operational SOW bullets to include in vendor agreements:
- Resource provisioning timeline (lead time for additional reserved units)
- Downtime notification window and planned maintenance windows (avoid business hours)
- Data handling: retention, deletion on contract end, and audit log exports
- Performance regression process: how new model versions are validated against a customer prompt set and rollback policy

Competitive notes (short, not exhaustive):
- Most cloud providers expose GPU endpoints but vary on isolation (shared pools vs dedicated nodes). They often punt on p99 guarantees at high sequence lengths.
- Self-hosted ops vendors promise isolation but lack a unified SLA with credits and predictable multi-region fallbacks.
- Our advantage to emphasize: unified contract across hosted/dedicated/private with clear fallbacks and tooling to measure token-level cost/latency.

Common questions & rebuttals (prep for sales calls):
Q: "Why not just use general-purpose GPUs on cloud IaaS?"
A: "Dedicated inference from a single vendor gives predictable kernels, automatic KV management, and a service-level contract that ties model performance to real cost — cloud IaaS leaves optimization, batching, and regression testing to you."

Q: "How do you prove isolation?"
A: "We provide architecture diagrams, audited separation controls, live demonstration of tenant logs, and optional on-prem deployment for auditors."

Quick field checklist before handing to procurement: (ticklist)
- [ ] Baseline performance artifact: p95/p99 over 7-day window at target seq length
- [ ] Security pack: SOC2 report / KMS integration summary
- [ ] Contract language: throughput and remedy paragraphs inserted
- [ ] Escalation contacts: named SRE and account lead
- [ ] Pricing add-ons: burst blocks, additional reserved units, cross-region replication

Open risks and unresolved items (notes for pricing/legal):
- How to price multi-region redundancy with strict throughput SLAs? (do we price per-region reserved units or a geo-redundant multiplier?)
- Standard credit formula for partial degradations (e.g., p95 OK but p99 missed) — need legal sign-off on tiered credits vs binary uptime.
- Auditability: what export format do customers need for forensic review? CSV? Parquet?

Appendix: field-ready email template to procurement (one paragraph)
"We appreciate the opportunity to partner on your inference needs. Attached is a baseline performance report and a draft SLA that maps our dedicated capacity to your throughput and isolation requirements. We'd recommend a 3-month ramp with a 30-minute daily burst window and a defined rollback policy for model updates. Happy to set a session with our platform architect to walk through the telemetry and the proposed contract language."

Notes to self / To follow up:
- Align with product on the sample throughput numbers for the mid-range reserved SKU.
- Get legal to finalize a credit schedule template and a fallback gravity clause for model mismatch events.
- Loop in SRE on audit export formats and retention defaults.

End.
